Figure 1:Overview of WorldMemBench. Top: case coverage across humans, objects,
environments, and dynamic events. Bottom left: controlled departure-and-revisit
evaluation compares each return against a fixed initial reference. Bottom right: capability profiles
of nine video world models.

Figure 2:Composition and diversity of WorldMemBench.(a)Case taxonomy, with Human, Object, Environment, and Dynamic categories in the inner ring and subcategories in the outer ring.(b)Case counts for static memory, dynamic memory, general video quality, and camera-following evaluation.(c)Representative cases showing target boxes and masks, scene depth, and event states before and after revisiting.

Figure 3:Evaluation camera trajectories in WorldMemBench.
Translation preserves the initial viewing direction and completes a square loop (green), while Rotation keeps the camera position fixed and applies left–right yaw (orange) or up–down pitch (blue).
Figure 4:Qualitative comparison of video world models on an environment case.
Figure 6:Qualitative comparison of video world models on a human case.
Figure 7:Qualitative comparison of video world models on an object case.
Figure 8:Blinded A/B preference annotation interface for Static Memory.
Figure 9:Event-gated checklist annotation interface for Dynamic Memory.

Figure 10:World memory under different context-access policies
in LingBot World v2.The examples depict (a) slicing a pepper, (b) performing a deadlift,
and (c) erasing a drawing.
Within each example, rows show Sliding Windows, FoV, and FullKV
from top to bottom.
Columns present selected frames along the prescribed LR-Hold
trajectory, spanning the initial observation, departure, and revisit.
Camera phases and frame indices are indicated above.
